en: Points of Controversy The Chapter on Refutation The Seventeenth Section
The Discussion on Whether There is an Accumulation of Merit for an Arahant:
Is there an accumulation of merit for an Arahant?
Yes, [they say].
Is there an accumulation of demerit for an Arahant?
One should not say so …pe… Is there no accumulation of demerit for an Arahant?
“Yes.
“Then there is no accumulation of merit for an Arahant?
“One should not say that,” and so on.
Is there an accumulation of merit for an arahant? Yes.
Does an arahant perform a volitional formation of merit, perform a volitional formation of the imperturbable, or [perform] that which leads to rebirth in a state of existence?
Does one perform kamma? Does one perform kamma that leads to existence? Does one perform kamma that leads to sovereignty? Does one perform kamma that leads to lordship?
Does one perform kamma that leads to great wealth? Does one perform kamma that leads to a large retinue?
Does one perform kamma that leads to divine fortune? Does one perform kamma that leads to human fortune?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there an accumulation of merit for an Arahant? Yes.
Does an Arahant accumulate [kamma]?
One should not say so... pe ...
Does an Arahant disintegrate [kamma]?
It should not be said thus...
[and so on] ...that an Arahant abandons...
[and so on] ...that an Arahant grasps... [and so on].
“The Arahant sweeps away,” ...
“the Arahant throws out,” ...
“the Arahant shakes off,” ... [and so on].
“Does an arahant blow up [the fires]?
One should not say so...
Is it not the case that an arahant neither accumulates nor diminishes, but stands having already diminished [them]?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If it is so, and the Arahant neither accumulates nor diminishes, but stands having ceased all accumulation, then surely it should not be said:
‘There is an accumulation of merit for the Arahant.’”

Is it not the case that the Arahant neither abandons nor grasps, but stands having abandoned; neither sinks down nor rises up, but stands having sunk down; neither fans out nor fans in, but stands having fanned out?
Yes, it is so.
If the Arahant neither fans out nor fans in, but stands having fanned out, then indeed, sir, you should not say—
“There is an accumulation of merit for an Arahant. Is it not the case that there is no accumulation of merit for an Arahant?
Yes, [it is].
“An Arahant might give a gift,” [you say]. “Yes.
Well then, if an Arahant might give a gift, surely it should not be said: [that he has no need for anything].
“There is no accumulation of merit for an arahant.
Yet an arahant might give a robe … or give almsfood.
One should provide lodging;
one should provide medicinal requisites for the sick;
one should provide solid food.
One should give solid food … one should give drinking water … one should pay homage to a shrine …
One might offer a garland at a cetiya,
offer incense, offer ointment, and so forth...
“Should an arahant perform a circumambulation of a cetiya?
“Yes.
If an arahant performs a circumambulation of a cetiya, then indeed, it should not be said: [that an arahant does not perform such acts].
“There is no accumulation of merit for an arahant.
The discussion on whether there is an accumulation of merit for an arahant is concluded.
